scope: Optional frozen PQ codebook backend in native.rs only; existing fresh Rust training remains the default. No native host operations.
api: write_native_with_codebook(directory, vectors, graph, pq_chunks, threads, seed, Option<&Path>)
behavior: Validate saved table dimension, chunk count, exactly 256 centers and finite effective absolute pivots before copying into the owned generation.
Retain raw codebook bytes. Load via existing PQStorage, convert BasicTable to TransposedTable, and compress all vectors with Rust QuantDataGenerator and a saved-codebook QuantCompressor.
Legacy C++ centering is handled by the existing loader. No C++ process or binary is invoked.
None delegates to existing write_native fresh-training behavior. copy_codebook also works when a small or empty base uses exact search.

validation.scope: Cross-compilation check only; not a Linux execution test.

tests: Both u8 and f32 native round trips: frozen codebook bytes and all unchanged-row compressed codes remain identical despite a changed seed; a modified row receives donor codes and queries at exact distance zero.
Bundled legacy C++ SIFT fixture: all Rust-generated compressed-code bytes exactly match existing C++ compressed-code bytes, and retained pivot bytes match.
Wrong dimension/chunk count, truncated input and a valid 128-center table are rejected before destination publication; same-path copy is safe.
Runtime-safe construction/search/drop, known Tokio blocking-worker guard, singleton-label graph and finite scalar validation remain covered.
failure_safety: Lifecycle callers write into a fresh private staging generation. Validation/copy/compression/layout failures return before prepared generation or CURRENT publication. Prior committed codebook is only read. Same canonical source/destination skips self-copy.
limits: Codebook reuse removes retraining drift but does not assert any unmeasured recall, latency or production guarantee.
